What do you do with all the poop? Do you just wash it into the nearest stream like every other place out there?

Uh, no, not any streams. We go through a solid 4 icecream tubs of poo a day, at least. We have a company that comes and picks up the poo (yeah we save it, very bad for the environment) they recycle it/make it fertilizer.

100 dogs is an average day, the average dog takes two poops a day, so we recycle 200 piles of dog poop a day of varying sizes. It's a glorious job sometimes.

How do you handle a fight? and what if one of the dogs is injured?

What is the best way to communicate with 40+ dogs when you don't know if they are friendly, irritated, hungry, etc; what is the one thing among dogs that make them listen?

Thanks for doing the AMA!

We split them up ;) seriously though, dogs rarely actually fight, then tend to make a lot of noise and snap a lot but rarely get in real damaging fights. When they do though its all hands on deck, if simply yelling "hey" doesn't break them up (90% of the time it does), then we start doing other things. First and foremost, if a bucket of water isn't close by you go for a dogs back legs, right near the hip/groin there is a pressure point, as long as you keep your head out of the way dogs will definitely release if pull backward this way. I've never had a fight that I couldn't split up within 15 seconds.

If a dog is injured badly enough we immediately take them to a vet, if not we contact the owner and let them know what happened. The owner of the injured dog pays, we have our clients sign a waiver for this very reason. Regardless of who hurt the dog it is still your responsibility not ours, or the other dogs owner's.

Same way you communicate with your dog at home. A shallow stomach/losing weight can mean a dog is hungry. If a dog is irritated there are some tell tale sign, low tail wagging, hackles up, growling, whale eye, stiff as a post are generally the things we look for in aggressive animals. Food.
